name: Equol (S-equol supplements, by mouth)
short: S-equol: a whole-body rash in a 134-woman trial; no serious effects in 160 women. With genistein and daidzein: more events (85% mild); vaginal bleeding in 1 and 3 on two doses, 0 on placebo.
text: In a 12-week randomised placebo-controlled trial in 134 Japanese women aged 40 to 59 given an S-equol supplement, no adverse effects were reported except a whole-body (systemic) rash in one woman in the higher-dose group. In a 12-week multicentre double-blind trial in 160 postmenopausal Japanese women who did not produce equol, no changes in clinical parameters or serious adverse effects were reported with S-equol; the abstract does not say whether milder effects occurred. In a prospective observational study of 74 middle-aged Japanese women who took an equol-containing supplement by mouth for a year, there were no reported adverse events and no abnormal findings in blood chemistry, cervical smear, mammography or transvaginal ultrasound; the abstract describes no comparison group. In a 12-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 101 postmenopausal Japanese women who did not produce equol, vaginal cell tests, womb-lining thickness and mammograms were done before and after treatment with S-equol, and the abstract reports no abnormal results in hormone status or gynaecological examinations. A 2019 systematic review of equol trials for hot flushes lists adverse events among its outcomes but does not report them in its abstract. In a different product, a formulation of genistein, daidzein and S-equol, a 12-week randomised trial in 71 perimenopausal women found adverse events in 16.7% on placebo, 39.1% on the lower dose and 29.2% on the higher dose; 85% were mild and none was severe, and vaginal bleeding occurred in none on placebo, one on the lower dose and three on the higher dose. Interactions: in an open-label crossover study in 24 healthy postmenopausal women, an S-equol-containing supplement taken for 7 days had no clinically significant effect on blood levels of anastrozole, letrozole, exemestane or tamoxifen, hormone drugs used for breast cancer.
